artigo.texto: 17/11/2026 - 13:00 As restrições dos Estados Unidos à exportação de chips de inteligência artificial podem atrasar projetos de data centers no Brasil e adiar parte da demanda por equipamentos da WEG (WEGE3), avalia o Bradesco BBI. O banco considera a notícia negativa para a fabricante de motores e equipamentos, mas mantém suas projeções, a recomendação equivalente à compra e o preço-alvo de R$ 62 por ação. A dimensão do impacto ainda é incerta e dependerá das características de cada projeto. Restrições a chips podem adiar investimentos em data centers Desde 16 de novembro, fornecedores precisam de autorização do governo americano para exportar ao Brasil determinados processadores utilizados em data centers. As exigências alcançam componentes fabricados fora dos Estados Unidos quando desenvolvidos com tecnologia americana. O objetivo de Washington é impedir que empresas chinesas utilizem operações em outros países para contornar as restrições tecnológicas impostas à China. A regulamentação do Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) citada na análise classifica Brasil, Singapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia como países com risco acima do normal de desvio ilegal desses componentes para China e Macau. Para o BBI, as exigências podem desacelerar a implantação de projetos no momento em que o governo brasileiro tenta atrair investimentos por meio do programa ReData. Como a WEG fornece equipamentos para esse mercado, eventuais adiamentos poderiam postergar encomendas. O banco ressalta que as regras não representam uma proibição total das exportações para o Brasil. Há exceções para operações ligadas a empresas americanas. O efeito dependerá da estrutura societária dos projetos, dos usuários finais dos chips e das aplicações pretendidas. Dados da Abinee, citados pelo BBI, mostram que as importações brasileiras de semicondutores atingiram US$ 6,8 bilhões entre janeiro e setembro, avanço de 51% na comparação anual. JPMorgan eleva preço-alvo da WEG para R$ 66 Em sua análise sobre a companhia, o JPMorgan reiterou a recomendação overweight, equivalente à compra, e elevou o preço-alvo da WEG de R$ 56 para R$ 66 ao fim de 2027. O novo valor representa um potencial de valorização de aproximadamente 30% em relação aos níveis considerados no relatório. A expectativa do banco é de aceleração do crescimento, sustentada principalmente pelos negócios de transformadores, sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias (BESS) e motores elétricos. Exposição internacional favorece a WEG com real mais fraco O JPMorgan destaca a proteção natural da companhia diante da desvalorização do real. Mais de 60% das receitas da WEG são geradas fora do Brasil, com cerca de 30% provenientes da América do Norte. Pelos cálculos do banco, cada depreciação de 5% do real acrescenta aproximadamente 4% ao EBITDA projetado da empresa. Após incorporar um cenário de câmbio mais depreciado, o JPMorgan elevou em 6% sua estimativa de EBITDA para 2027. A projeção passou a considerar crescimento de 27% nessa linha. O banco prevê receitas e lucro líquido acima do consenso de mercado em 2027 e 2028. Banco vê desconto nos múltiplos de WEGE3 Na avaliação do JPMorgan, a ação da WEG negocia a múltiplos atrativos, com desconto de aproximadamente 15% em relação à média histórica do período pós-pandemia. Os analistas argumentam que a companhia tende a se beneficiar da exposição ao dólar e da menor dependência do ciclo econômico brasileiro. Esses atributos, associados à percepção de qualidade da empresa, sustentam a visão favorável do banco para WEGE3. artigo.texto: O governo da Bolívia iniciou negociações com o Kawari Fund para estruturar a venda de créditos de carbono provenientes da preservação florestal, transformando a manutenção de ecossistemas em um fluxo de receita financeira direta. O mecanismo, discutido durante a COP31, visa conectar investidores internacionais às comunidades indígenas que atuam na vigilância e proteção dos recursos naturais. A operação baseia-se na iniciativa REDD+ (Redução de Emissões por Desmatamento e Degradação florestal), que atrai capital estrangeiro mediante a comprovação da redução de emissões de gases de efeito estufa. O projeto piloto foi concentrado no Distrito Autônomo Indígena Charua Iyambae, onde a fase atual consiste em consultas obrigatórias para garantir a conformidade dos direitos das comunidades locais antes da implementação do fluxo financeiro. Para viabilizar a atratividade do ativo para os compradores de créditos, o Ministro da Produção Sustentável, Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos, Oscar Mario Justiniano, trabalha na criação de uma estrutura de governança que elimine intermediários. O objetivo é que o pagamento pelos créditos de carbono chegue diretamente ao orçamento das famílias que operam como patrulhas florestais. Segundo Vanessa Jiménez, representante do Kawari Fund, a transparência nos relatórios de destino dos fundos é a condição necessária para que investidores internacionais mantenham o aporte de capital no país. A conversão da floresta em ativo financeiro depende de um processo de verificação técnica, conduzido pela Fundação Amigos da Natureza (FAN) e pela União Internacional para a Conservação da Natureza (CI). Essas entidades são responsáveis pelo monitoramento e a certificação da quantidade de carbono sequestrado, etapa indispensável para que as empresas compradoras possam registrar legalmente as cotas em seus balanços de emissões. Caso o modelo piloto no distrito Charua Iyambae seja validado, a Bolívia pretende expandir a escala da operação, estabelecendo um preço por tonelada de CO2 absorvido que se converta em renda estável para as populações residentes nas áreas florestais. artigo.texto: The Commerce Department on Monday moved to close a loophole that has let Chinese companies lease Nvidia's advanced computing power from data centers in third countries, effectively circumventing controls on sensitive chip technology being exported to China. The interim final rule from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security is the first U.S. policy response to the scandal that led Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign last week after reports that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who worked for Megaspeed, one of Nvidia's biggest Asian customers. The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release. The rule came after growing criticism of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for not doing enough to prevent possible diversion of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China in violation of American export controls. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in an interview on Friday with CNBC's "Squawk Box," blamed the Commerce Department for not putting Singapore-based Megaspeed on its "entity list," which would restrict certain exports to it. Share prices of Nvidia and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence trade fell Monday morning after the interim rule was announced, among them chipmakers Micron Technology, Intel and Advanced Micro Devices. The rule is designed "to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests," according to the text of the rule. The new restrictions "will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using" advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors produced by U.S. companies to train advanced AI models, the rule says. The rule also says that a license will now "be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs) – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion." The New York Times reported on Nov. 9 that American authorities began investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed and one of its executives, Alice Huang, in 2024, "after the company started importing billions of dollars' worth of advanced Nvidia A.I. equipment into Malaysia." "Megaspeed had been planning and constructing data centers around Southeast Asia to serve Chinese clients, including Alibaba, the Chinese tech giant," The Times reported that day. "While that behavior is legal, U.S. officials were concerned that some of the Nvidia chips the company had bought were illegally routed into China." Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week after reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, and that she was a spy working for China. The two are not related. China's government has denied the claim that Alice Huang was a spy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who, as national security advisor, leads the National Security Council, warned President Donald Trump last spring that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, The Times has reported. Rep. John Mooelnaar, the Michigan Republican who is chairman of the House Select Committee on China, in a statement on the new rule that it "sends a message to the Chinese Communist Party that America is serious about closing dangerous export control loopholes China has been exploiting for years." "Our most advanced AI chips are simply not for sale to our foremost enemy," Moolenaar said. "This new rule is an important step in keeping chips out of ill-intentioned hands, strengthens our national security laws, and will help protect America's lead in the AI race." Chris McGuire, a former deputy senior director for technology and national security at the National Security Council, in a post on X called the new rule "a major step forward to countering Chinese smuggling of and access to advanced AI chips." "The work here is not done, as there are some critical loopholes that remain open and need to be closed in a follow-up rule (namely those related to activities inside the United States)," wrote McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. "Commerce should move extremely quickly to close these. But this is the first time in over 18 months that the administration is starting to take export controls seriously, and does represent a meaningful step forward." McGuire said that the fact that the new rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the NSC "is remarkable and unprecedented." "I have never seen a BIS rule that was not written by BIS," he wrote. "That implies that Commerce was dragged kicking and screaming over the finish line by the White House and Treasury, and instructed to publish this rule rather than the rumored weaker one that it preferred. Remarkable." Commerce's new rule was published a day after Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington state, the ranking Democrat on the Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, in a letter to Lutnick said that Chinese companies such as Alibaba and ByteDance have "used overseas data centers equipped with advanced Nvidia chips to train advanced AI models." "These companies are exploiting a loophole in U.S. export controls by using advanced American chips in foreign data centers even when those chips are restricted from the [People's Republic of China]," Cantwell wrote. "Despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security that certain arrangements may violate existing restrictions, the Department of Commerce failed to close this loophole, allowing PRC companies to advance their AI capabilities using sensitive American technology," she wrote.

The new restrictions "will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using" advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors produced by U.S. companies to train advanced AI models, the rule says. The rule also says that a license will now "be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs) – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion." The New York Times reported on Nov. 9 that American authorities began investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed and one of its executives, Alice Huang, in 2024, "after the company started importing billions of dollars' worth of advanced Nvidia A.I. equipment into Malaysia." "Megaspeed had been planning and constructing data centers around Southeast Asia to serve Chinese clients, including Alibaba, the Chinese tech giant," The Times reported that day. "While that behavior is legal, U.S. officials were concerned that some of the Nvidia chips the company had bought were illegally routed into China." Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week after reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, and that she was a spy working for China. The two are not related. China's government has denied the claim that Alice Huang was a spy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who, as national security advisor, leads the National Security Council, warned President Donald Trump last spring that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, The Times has reported. Rep. John Mooelnaar, the Michigan Republican who is chairman of the House Select Committee on China, in a statement on the new rule that it "sends a message to the Chinese Communist Party that America is serious about closing dangerous export control loopholes China has been exploiting for years." "Our most advanced AI chips are simply not for sale to our foremost enemy," Moolenaar said. "This new rule is an important step in keeping chips out of ill-intentioned hands, strengthens our national security laws, and will help protect America's lead in the AI race." Chris McGuire, a former deputy senior director for technology and national security at the National Security Council, in a post on X called the new rule "a major step forward to countering Chinese smuggling of and access to advanced AI chips." "The work here is not done, as there are some critical loopholes that remain open and need to be closed in a follow-up rule (namely those related to activities inside the United States)," wrote McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. "Commerce should move extremely quickly to close these. But this is the first time in over 18 months that the administration is starting to take export controls seriously, and does represent a meaningful step forward." McGuire said that the fact that the new rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the NSC "is remarkable and unprecedented." "I have never seen a BIS rule that was not written by BIS," he wrote. "That implies that Commerce was dragged kicking and screaming over the finish line by the White House and Treasury, and instructed to publish this rule rather than the rumored weaker one that it preferred. Remarkable." Commerce's new rule was published a day after Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington state, the ranking Democrat on the Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, in a letter to Lutnick said that Chinese companies such as Alibaba and ByteDance have "used overseas data centers equipped with advanced Nvidia chips to train advanced AI models." "These companies are exploiting a loophole in U.S. export controls by using advanced American chips in foreign data centers even when those chips are restricted from the [People's Republic of China]," Cantwell wrote. "Despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security that certain arrangements may violate existing restrictions, the Department of Commerce failed to close this loophole, allowing PRC companies to advance their AI capabilities using sensitive American technology," she wrote.

artigo.texto: From emission pricing to green investment incentives Within the framework of the 31st Conference of Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), Vietnam launched its Carbon Market Information Portal, marking another step forward in perfecting the infrastructure and operational mechanisms of the market. The public disclosure of information on policies, regulations, and trading activities is expected to facilitate access to the market for businesses and investors, while also promoting the mobilization of resources for emission reduction activities. Previously, on June 29, 2026, the Vietnam Carbon Exchange officially launched at the Hanoi Stock Exchange, along with the commissioning of the National Registration System for Greenhouse Gas Emission Quotas and Carbon Credits. The gradual completion of the market's components lays the foundation for transparent trading, establishes a carbon pricing mechanism, and encourages businesses to invest in emission reduction solutions. According to the plan, approximately 511 million tons of CO₂, equivalent to the approved emission quota, will be allocated on a pilot basis during the 2025-2026 period to 110 facilities in three sectors: thermal power, iron and steel production, and cement. These are all energy-intensive industries with a high demand for production line modernization and the adoption of emission reduction technologies. Including these facilities in the quota allocation mechanism not only increases their responsibility for emission control but also forces businesses to reassess the long-term effectiveness of their investments. According to Mr. Bui Duc Hieu, Deputy Director of the Climate Change Department, carbon credits are not only a tool for managing emissions but also an incentive for businesses to innovate technology, use energy efficiently, and invest in emission reduction solutions. However, for the market to play this role, perfecting the legal framework and technical infrastructure needs to go hand in hand with improving the quality of emission measurement, reporting, and assessment, as well as the capacity of businesses to participate. When emission costs are factored into production calculations, businesses have more incentive to innovate technologically, save energy, and improve investment efficiency. Units maintaining energy-intensive production lines may face increased compliance costs; while businesses that proactively improve processes and reduce emissions will have an advantage in cost control and production organization. This also encourages capital flows towards clean technology projects, efficient energy use, and sustainable production development. Furthermore, the carbon quota and credit trading mechanism opens up the possibility of generating additional revenue from emission reduction results that meet the conditions for recognition and transfer . Although this revenue depends on regulations, trading capacity, and market price fluctuations, the prospect of commercializing emission reduction results can become a factor for businesses to consider when developing investment plans. Through this, the carbon market gradually links environmental goals with economic benefits, creating further incentives for businesses to transform their production models towards low emissions. Market transparency to unlock capital flows. Along with the establishment of carbon pricing mechanisms, the ability to mobilize resources for emission reduction projects is becoming a matter of concern. The demand for investment in technological innovation, improved energy efficiency, and the use of clean fuels is growing, while many businesses still face difficulties in balancing capital, especially for projects with high initial costs and long payback periods. The development of the carbon market is therefore expected to create additional financial incentives, supporting businesses in implementing the green transition process. According to John Robert Cotton, Director of the Energy Transition Partnership (ETP) for Southeast Asia at UNOPS, very few countries have been able to transition from establishing a legal framework to operating a mandatory carbon market in such a short time as Vietnam. He believes that carbon pricing is crucial in incorporating emission costs into businesses' financial calculations, thereby creating incentives for investment in emission reduction. Notably, from 2029, when the quota auction mechanism is expected to be implemented, the market could generate additional budget revenue for reinvestment in emission reduction activities in industry. Besides domestic resources, international cooperation also opens opportunities to mobilize financing for green transition. Through cooperation mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, projects that meet emission reduction requirements can access financing from the international carbon market. However, the ability to attract capital depends on the quality of the project, the transparency of emission reduction results, and compliance with transaction standards. While the carbon market opens up opportunities to mobilize resources, the ability to convert these opportunities into actual investment capital still depends on the financial efficiency of each project. From a credit perspective, Mr. Bui Minh Giap, Chief Economist of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Vietnam, said that Vietnam needs approximately US$368 billion in additional investment capital by 2040 to adapt to climate change, enhance resilience, and reduce emissions, equivalent to 6.8% of GDP per year. Specifically in the electricity sector, the investment needs for developing power sources and grids in the 2026-2030 period, according to the revised Power Development Plan VIII, are estimated at around US$136 billion. artigo.texto: The Duxbury Planning Board is looking to offer next year’s Town Meeting up to six new or updated zoning laws, including regulations for battery energy storage systems, members announced this week. On Monday at the Selectboard’s meeting at Town Hall, Planning Board Chairwoman Kristin Rappe said members of her committee had been meeting weekly to ready the zoning alterations for the March 13, 2027 Town Meeting. One of the more consequential proposals is a new bylaw to regulate battery energy storage systems. Known as BESS, these systems use lithium-ion batteries to store electricity, most often produced from renewable sources, and release it to the power grid when the energy is needed during peak usage hours. In Duxbury, a plan to put a BESS on residentially zoned land on West Street last year caused an uproar with hundreds of residents objecting to it. Proponents did not move forward with that project, but the experience showed the Planning Board that it needed to find a way to regulate BESS, since the state’s clean energy regulations require the town to address these systems. While the town can’t prohibit BESS in Duxbury, it can pass a law that sets town standards to protect the health and safety of residents, said Rappe. Passing regulations does not mean the town is welcoming these systems, said Selectboard member Brian Glennon. The proposed bylaw would establish regulations for siting a BESS on land in town. These include setbacks and screening required for when the system is built, safety mechanisms for when it is running and a decommissioning and financial surety for when it would no longer be in service. Many battery energy storage systems are large and take up multiple acres. One of the newest and the largest is in Medway and was completed this year. That site is 10.6 acres with the BESS taking up 5.2 acres and producing 250 MW, according to the state Department of Public Utilities. Duxbury’s proposed BESS zoning law could limit these systems to lots that are at least 250,000 square feet, or nearly six acres. This is because the system would be required to have 200-foot setbacks on all sides with a minimum lot size of 500 by 500 feet. The locations would also be required to have a perimeter buffer and fencing, access roads large enough for fire trucks and a water cistern and fire hydrant. Also, no BESS could be sited in the Dunes, Flood Hazard, Wetlands Protection, Aquifer Protection or Waterfront Scene Area overlay districts. Rappe said the Planning Board studied other towns’ regulations before writing its own. Also, board members kept two principles in mind for the new rules: They must not endanger the health, safety and welfare of residents and they must protect the environment. In addition, the new zoning proposal needed to meet three tests, she said. These include adoption at Town Meeting, approval by the state Attorney General and being defensible in court. “There is a very long list of things we’ve done to try to make sure that Duxbury and its citizens are kept safe,” she said. “The consequences of not passing it are that we have no local regulations, no control, and it could be sited almost anywhere.” This bylaw is not to encourage BESS in town but to have a process to regulate them if they are proposed, said Rappe. The Planning Board held a public information session on BESS on Nov. 16. Selectboard members had a few questions for the Planning Board on the BESS bylaw but they praised the effort so far. “Great job,” said Glennon, “You’ve done a lot of hard work on this.” “We need to put something in place even if we abhor to have to do this,” said Selectboard Vice Chairman Fernando Guitart. “When it comes to town, at least we have some measure of control, so that’s going to be the key selling point. We have to convince Town Meeting.” In addition to the BESS bylaw, the Planning Board is proposing five other law changes. One of the less complicated proposals includes updates to certain sections of the town’s current zoning law to ensure the language is consistent with changes to Chapter 40A, the state law that regulates local zoning bylaws. That law was updated in July. A second proposal amends the existing Flood Hazard Area Overlay District as specified by the Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation. According to Rappe, this action will not affect residents’ flood insurance. The board is also proposing to update over 60 definitions and terms in the zoning bylaw. Many are language updates such as changing the term “Board of Appeals” to “Zoning Board of Appeals” or changing “Chairman” to “Chair.” There are two other more substantial zoning bylaw changes. One is to update the Inclusionary Housing section to encourage more affordable housing and the other would replace the Residential Conservation Cluster zoning with something called the Open Space Residential Development District. Any zoning bylaws proposed for Town Meeting will be reviewed by both the Selectboard and Planning Board at public hearings before the meeting.

artigo.texto: South Korea's Mplus Wins approximately $15 Million Solid-State Battery Assembly and Electrode Equipment Order from Global Battery Maker Mplus, a South Korean specialist in secondary-battery assembly equipment, has won an order worth approximately 20 billion won (approximately $15.0 million) from a global battery company for assembly and electrode-line equipment used in solid-state battery mass production. According to industry sources on the 16th, the contract covers equipment for the customer's solid-state battery production line, and its significance lies in Mplus securing an official supply track record in the next-generation battery mass-production equipment segment. The equipment to be supplied will use assembly machinery developed in-house by Mplus, incorporating core process technologies such as notching, stacking and precision dispensing. The company is also developing its own roll press technology capable of replacing the warm isostatic press (WIP), which is regarded as a representative pressing process for solid-state batteries. Through this, Mplus aims to build a full lineup of equipment covering all processes required for solid-state battery production. Solid-state batteries are next-generation secondary batteries that replace conventional liquid electrolytes with solid ones. They can improve safety and energy density, but their manufacturing processes are highly demanding, and equipment technology capable of supporting stable mass production is seen as the key to commercialization. As major automakers target the launch of vehicles equipped with solid-state batteries by 2030, battery manufacturers are accelerating facility investment in pilot and mass-production lines. Note: The counterparty and detailed delivery terms were not disclosed. Mplus is also accelerating the diversification of its order portfolio. After recently targeting the multi-purpose specialty battery equipment market, including defense applications, with a European global battery company, it has now also secured this solid-state equipment order, expanding its customer base from a focus on electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems (ESS) into next-generation and specialty battery segments. A company official said, "This order is meaningful in that we have secured an official supply reference in the next-generation solid-state battery mass-production equipment segment," adding, "If the customer's shift to solid-state battery mass production gets into full swing, it could lead to follow-on large orders." The official added, "We also expect additional order opportunities as the customer expands production going forward." Industry observers expect order opportunities for related equipment makers to expand as the solid-state battery market moves beyond the R&D stage into a phase of preparation for commercialization. In particular, they say a track record of supplying initial production lines could serve as a gauge of competitiveness in future mass-production equipment orders. Mplus manufactures assembly equipment — including notching, stacking, tab welding and packaging for pouch-type, prismatic and solid-state batteries — as well as electrode-line facilities. The company is also expanding its new business portfolio, including autonomous mobile robots (AIMRs) and control systems for the physical AI (artificial intelligence) era. This contract remains at the equipment supply stage, so its immediate contribution to earnings may be limited, but it is significant as a bridgehead for securing additional orders when the shift to solid-state battery mass production takes place. Solid-state batteries are still in the early stages of mass production and process standards have not yet been established, so companies that supply equipment for initial lines are seen as potentially holding an advantageous position in subsequent equipment orders. However, some note that with the customer unidentified and the mass-production schedule unconfirmed, whether follow-on orders materialize depends on the pace of the customer's investment execution. artigo.texto: NTT Eyes Space Optical Communications Network, Lunar Power Supply and Space Data Centers NTT President Akira Shimada said in a November 16 lecture in Tokyo that the company will build a space optical communications network linking satellites to each other and to ground communications equipment via optical signals. The company aims to mount electronic components compatible with its next-generation high-speed communications platform IOWN on satellites and other communications devices, creating a system that efficiently delivers satellite-acquired data to ground receiving stations by routing it through another satellite positioned closer to the receiver. Shimada also outlined plans to work on space data centers and power-generation infrastructure on the lunar surface. "NTT will use the technology it has cultivated to weave an optical information network across space," Shimada said, stressing the significance of extending the company's communications control technology into the space domain. Optical communications can transmit far larger volumes of data than radio waves, but are vulnerable to weather and atmospheric conditions, including blockage by clouds. NTT will need technology to accurately transmit data to satellites moving at speeds that circle the Earth in about 90 minutes, as well as the ability to select communications routes that connect multiple satellites and ground equipment along the shortest path. Shimada also said that "the major social roles space will play are communications and observation." Analyzing high-resolution imagery captured by satellites can be used to assess conditions during wildfires and disasters, as well as to survey the distribution of wildlife and vegetation. NTT also anticipates demand for satellite communications as a supplement in mountainous areas and remote islands where terrestrial networks are hard to reach. NTT plans to deploy ground communications equipment around the world by fiscal 2029. Partnership with ispace to study lunar infrastructure NTT announced the same day that it has signed a partnership agreement with space venture ispace (Chuo Ward, Tokyo). The two companies will pursue research, development, demonstration and study toward future commercialization of infrastructure technologies including high-speed optical communications in cislunar space—the region between Earth and the Moon—and wireless laser power transmission on the lunar surface. As lunar exploration advances, a wide variety of data will be generated, including sensor data and activity logs in addition to measurement data. Communications and power infrastructure will be essential to transmit this data to Earth and share it on the Moon as well. From an economic security standpoint, experts have also pointed to the importance of Japan taking the lead in building and managing such infrastructure. While expanding its optical communications research into space, NTT has been developing laser wireless power transmission technology with an eye toward applications beyond communications. ispace, through the lunar landers and rovers its group develops and operates, is working to provide lunar transportation and lunar data services. It plans "Mission 3," targeting a lunar landing in 2028, and aims to commercialize communications and positioning services using lunar orbiters, with plans to launch its first orbiter as early as 2027 under "Mission 2.5." The two companies will combine NTT's optical technologies, including optical communications and laser power transmission, with ispace's expertise in lunar transportation, exploration and mission operations to verify the applicability of optical technology to the lunar environment. Private-sector entry accelerates in U.S.-China-led space race The United States and China are vying for leadership in space development, with countries competing over the number of satellites launched. SpaceX, led by entrepreneur Elon Musk, is pursuing a plan to expand its satellite constellation to 42,000. China has set out a vision of deploying more than 200,000 satellites by the mid-2030s, and South Korea plans to build a network of 7,000 communications satellites. Major IT companies such as Amazon.com are also entering the field, intensifying competition over the use of low-Earth-orbit satellites. The concept of placing computing infrastructure in space is also gaining traction as an alternative to ground-based data centers, which are increasingly struggling to secure power and cooling water. NTT's space data center initiative is seen as aimed at capturing this demand. Market impact For NTT, space optical communications represent an attempt to open a new revenue stream from IOWN-related technology. With Japan's domestic communications market maturing, satellite communications and space infrastructure are drawing attention as areas with significant growth potential. If the partnership with ispace moves from demonstration to commercialization, it could raise the profile of Japanese companies in international competition over lunar transportation and data communications. At the same time, SpaceX and Chinese state-owned enterprises boast overwhelming launch volumes for low-Earth-orbit satellites, and international coordination over the use of frequencies and orbits remains a challenge. Putting an optical communications network into practical use requires the mass deployment of satellites and the buildout of ground equipment, raising questions about the scale of investment required. How NTT's expansion into space contributes to its earnings structure will depend on the progress of demonstrations and the timing of commercialization. artigo.texto: POSCO Signs 3-Year Lithium Supply Deal With CATL, Securing China's Battery Giant POSCO Group has signed a long-term lithium supply contract with China's CATL, the world's top player in the global electric vehicle battery market. According to POSCO Group on the 18th, the two companies agreed to a three-year contract to supply lithium used in EV battery manufacturing from 2026 through 2028, and shipments under the agreement are already underway. Specific volumes and the contract value were not disclosed. The deal gives POSCO Group a stable sales channel in China, the world's largest EV battery market. CATL holds about 40% of the global EV battery market and supplies batteries to automakers in China and around the world. A POSCO Group official said the two companies "agreed to work together to solidify a long-term partnership and build a stable raw material procurement system." Lithium is a core material directly tied to battery production costs, and its price is highly volatile, making stable sales channels critical for producers and raw material supply chain management critical for battery makers. The contract extends the strategy Chairman Chang In-hwa has emphasized: securing quality resources preemptively and diversifying global customers. POSCO Group has expanded its lithium business based on the raw material procurement and development capabilities it built in the steel business. After securing mining rights to Argentina's Hombre Muerto salt flat in 2018, it completed a 25,000-ton-per-year lithium hydroxide Plant 1 there in 2024, and in October it finished the raw material production facilities for brine lithium Plant 2. That site produces 23,000 tons of lithium carbonate a year, which is brought to the Yulchon Industrial Complex in Gwangyang, South Korea's South Jeolla Province, and refined into battery-grade lithium hydroxide. The Yulchon refinery, targeted for completion in the first quarter of next year, will have a capacity of 25,000 tons per year. Once completed, Argentina's brine-based lithium hydroxide capacity will rise to 50,000 tons per year. Adding the 43,000 tons of ore-based capacity secured at the Yulchon complex by POSCO Pilbara Lithium Solution, a joint venture with Australia's PLS Group, brings total capacity to 93,000 tons per year. POSCO Group plans to build Plants 3 and 4 in Argentina to expand local brine-based lithium product capacity to 100,000 tons per year by 2033. Note: Argentina Plant 2 produces 23,000 tons of lithium carbonate a year, which is brought to Yulchon and refined into lithium hydroxide. POSCO Group previously signed a long-term lithium supply contract with South Korea's SK On in February. It will supply up to 25,000 tons from this year through 2028, with the volumes destined for EV battery projects in Europe and North America. With a long-term customer among South Korean battery makers and now the global No. 1, POSCO Group's lithium sales channels span South Korea, China, Europe and North America. The contract illustrates how both raw material producers and demand-side companies are prioritizing supply chain stability amid growing lithium price volatility. POSCO Group aims to boost the profitability of its lithium business by expanding capacity and increasing long-term supply contracts with global battery makers. However, with volumes and value undisclosed, the specific impact of the deal on earnings has yet to be determined. artigo.texto: Trina Storage and the Swedish company OX2 signed a framework agreement for the supply of battery energy storage systems (BESS) with an approximate capacity of 3 GWh. The equipment will be used in projects in Finland, Sweden, Poland, and Italy, most of which are expected to become operational by 2028. The agreement is part of OX2 expansion of its European energy storage portfolio and includes standalone installations and hybrid solutions linked to renewable generation projects. According to the planned schedule, the projects will reach financial close between 2026 and 2027. Trina Storage will supply BESS systems in four European countries Trina Storage, Trinasolar’s energy storage division, will provide battery systems for various projects developed by OX2 in the European market. The agreement includes approximately 3 GWh of storage capacity, distributed among facilities located in Finland, Sweden, Poland and Italy. The collaboration will allow progress in the development of a portfolio of projects that combines stand-alone BESS systems with installations integrated into renewable energy plants. Although the companies have not detailed the individual capacity of each project or the economic value of the agreement, OX2 anticipates that most of the facilities will begin operating in 2028, once the financing, construction and commissioning stages are completed. These systems will allow electricity to be stored and supplied later according to the operational needs of the network. Energy storage is gaining importance in Europe The growing incorporation of solar and wind power generation there is a growing need for technologies that bring flexibility to European electricity systems. In this scenario, BESS systems allow energy to be stored for certain periods and supplied when generation or demand conditions require it. Furthermore, they can contribute to the stability of electrical networks through regulation and rapid response services, depending on the technical and commercial characteristics of each installation. For OX2, this technology represents a growth opportunity in both independent projects and hybrid solutions that combine renewable production and storage. Paolo Romanacci, OX2 operations director, highlighted that the company’s storage business continues to grow through both development methods. The executive also expressed his satisfaction at establishing a long-term collaboration with Trina Storage, which will allow progress in the execution of OX2 European project portfolio. OX2 expands its investments in solar energy and batteries in Poland The new collaboration with Trina Storage comes after OX2 announced further investments in renewable generation and energy storage in the Polish market. In June 2026, the company announced investment decisions for two projects, one being the Lion photovoltaic park and the other a battery storage facility in Osiek Jasielski. The Lion solar park, located in the municipality of Sława, in the Lubusz Voivodeship, will have a maximum capacity of 165 MWp and will be one of the largest photovoltaic projects developed by OX2 in Poland. Once operational, it is estimated to produce approximately 184 GWh of electricity per year, a volume equivalent to the annual consumption of about 51,000 homes, according to estimates announced by the company. Furthermore, Osiek Jasielski BESS installation will have a capacity of 50 MW and a storage capacity of 120 MWh. This project represents OX2’s first investment in battery storage in Poland. Both initiatives are part of the company’s expansion in the Polish electricity sector and reflect its interest in combining renewable generation assets with storage technologies. Finland promotes new high-capacity BESS systems Finland has also become a relevant market for OX2 growth in energy storage, in February 2026, the company reached a seven-year agreement with Statkraft for the optimization of two BESS facilities currently under construction. The projects will have a combined capacity of 235 MW and a total energy capacity of 470 MWh. One of the facilities will have 110 MW of power and 220 MWh of storage, while the second will have 125 MW and 250 MWh. Both systems will be located next to the Kannisto wind farm project in Halsua and the Korkeamaa wind farm project in Soini, and are scheduled to become operational in 2028. Under the terms of the agreement, Statkraft will take over the commercial optimization of the batteries, with the aim of managing its participation in the electricity market and taking advantage of the opportunities associated with system flexibility. These investments demonstrate the growth of OX2 storage portfolio in Northern Europe, where BESS systems are becoming increasingly important to complement renewable generation. The 3 GWh agreement reinforces OX2 expansion in Europe The alliance between Trina Storage and OX2 represents a new step in the development of large-scale energy storage projects in Europe. The planned supply of 3 GWh will support a significant part of the Swedish company’s European portfolio, while it moves forward with the financing and execution of new facilities. The financial closings planned between 2026 and 2027 will be crucial to completing the projects included in the agreement. With most of the facilities scheduled to become operational in 2028, the collaboration seeks to expand the availability of storage systems and strengthen the integration of renewable energy into the electricity markets of Finland, Sweden, Poland, and Italy. artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - BAIC Motor aims to free up capital through the sale, while its parent is working with CATL to bring more models onto the battery maker's swap network. - The assets have an appraised value of about 278 million yuan ($41.4 million). BAIC Motor (HKEX: 1958) plans to sell assets tied to 112 battery swap stations through a public tender to free up capital tied up in non-core assets. Its wholly owned subsidiary, BAIC Powertrain, plans to submit a notice of the proposed sale to the China Beijing Equity Exchange (CBEX) by the end of November, BAIC Motor said in a Hong Kong stock exchange filing on Tuesday. BAIC Powertrain plans to sell its entire interest in the assets, which include inventory, fixed assets, construction in progress and intangible assets used in station operations. A September 30 appraisal using the cost approach valued the assets at about 278 million yuan ($41.4 million), excluding tax, about 1.54% above their unaudited book value. The listing price will be at least as high as the appraised value ultimately filed with the authorities. The winning bid will determine the sale price. At the time of the filing, BAIC Powertrain had yet to identify a buyer or sign a sale agreement. BAIC Motor estimates that a sale at the appraised value in 2026 would lift its consolidated profit for the year by about 3.52 million yuan after transaction costs. BAIC Powertrain plans to use the proceeds to fund its operations and development. The proposed sale comes as BAIC Motor's parent, Beijing Automotive Group (BAIC Group), expands its battery swap partnership with CATL (HKEX: 3750). BAIC Group said in October that it would bring compatible models from several of its brands onto CATL's Choco swap network and make dealership sites available for new swap stations. The partners aim to serve 1 million vehicles. On November 13, BAIC Group's Arcfox brand launched a LiDAR-equipped battery swap version of the Beta S3 and a battery swap version of the Beta T1. Both use CATL's battery swap system for passenger vehicles. Arcfox said it would offer a battery swap version of every model in its lineup next year. Battery swap stations are expensive for automakers to build and maintain, BAIC Group chairman Zhang Jianyong said at the launch. Battery makers can benefit from economies of scale in both construction and operation, he said. BAIC began researching battery swap technology in 2011, making it one of the first automakers in China to invest in the field, Zhang said. He said BAIC Group and CATL would draw on their respective strengths to build China's first battery swap network capable of serving about 1 million vehicles. ($1 = 6.7118 yuan)

artigo.texto: Today’s ESG Updates - Data Centers Emitting on the Scale of a Country: A study by a team of Harvard researchers analyzed electricity use at the largest data centers and estimated 28.3 million tons of carbon produced. - Tough Negotiations on Climate Change at COP31: Nearly 200 countries at the conference appear unable to agree on climate mitigation strategies, as the first draft was rejected by some countries the same day. - EU Sets Tariffs on Steel, Mostly From Asia: The EU is imposing tariffs on cold-rolled flat steel products from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey, and Vietnam; the duties take effect Tuesday, November 17. - Proposal to Ease ESG Reporting Rules Met With Disagreement: The European Union faces criticism over a proposal to relax sustainability reporting requirements for companies headquartered outside the bloc. New study shows the true scale of data center emissions Harvard researchers examined 403 of the largest U.S. data centers over a year, between May 2024 and April 2025. The estimated numbers: 28.3 million tons of carbon dioxide and 82 terawatt-hours of electricity from fossil fuels. The first reactions from the expert community agree that the estimate is realistic. Despite claiming that carbon-free power is essential for data centers, former U.S. Vice President and climate activist Al Gore argued that there is hope. In his opinion, advanced AI will eventually help find ways to use energy more efficiently. Another potential upside is the heat coming from data centers; capturing it can provide heat to homes and businesses in the area. The International Energy Agency estimates that by 2030 this can be the heat source for 10% of European homes. Klimado – Navigating climate complexity just got easier. Klimado offers a user-friendly platform for tracking local and global environmental shifts, making it an essential tool for climate-aware individuals and organizations. COP31 heated negotiations reflect the year of heatwaves COP31 negotiators published a draft deal on Monday, with the main gaps between countries including fossil fuels and climate financing. Country representatives need to reach an agreement by the end of this week. Australia’s Chris Bowen, who is leading the negotiation, said some countries have already rejected the latest 18-page draft. The event reflects a year of global warming that caused wildfires in Europe and glacier melting in Nepal. Other crises, like wars and the rising cost of living, limit political motivation. The annual UN climate talks seem unable to reach consensus among almost 200 nations. At the same time, the situation is dire: the latest UN report said the world is on course to exceed the 1.5 °C threshold for the worst climate change effects. Related Articles Here is a list of articles selected by our Editorial Board that have gained significant interest from the public: EU imposes duties on steel to balance prices The new tariffs follow the bloc’s findings that steel products from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey, and Vietnam were sold at unfairly low prices. The rates are set at 9.5% for Indian producers, 27.9% for Japanese steelmakers, and up to 20.7% for Taiwanese companies. The total EU market for cold-rolled flat steel is around €23.2 billion, while imports from the now-tariffed countries accounted for about €1.78 billion. Dumping duties like these typically come from comparing producers’ domestic sales prices. However, that applies only to normally functioning markets. For example, the EU uses a normal value for Chinese products outside the country. Here, the European Commission stated that government measures distorted Indian domestic prices. Easing ESG reporting for non-EU companies becomes an unpopular proposal An initiative to ease ESG requirements for companies headquartered outside of the bloc was backed by U.S. business lobbying groups. Naturally, its main aim was to decrease the regulatory burden for international business. The proposal has sparked a dispute around the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), which requires disclosure on environmental, social, and governance impacts. The European Commission suggests a mixed approach for non-EU companies that could potentially narrow their global reporting requirements. According to the proposal, international companies would have more limited requirements on worldwide impacts but would keep the requirements for products and services inside the EU. This suggestion has encountered opposition within the bloc. The main dilemma is maintaining ambitious disclosure standards to protect competitive fairness for European companies. ___________________________________________________________________________________ Editor’s Note: The opinions expressed here by the authors are their own, not those of impakter.com — Cover Photo Credit: Chad Davis

Under the Japanese POWERR Asia initiative, ASEAN nations would be able to use Japan’s excess storage capacity for crude oil. “We have suggested to utilize our crude oil stockpiling facilities in Japan, which is not utilized,” Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs press secretary Toshihiro Kitamura told reporters on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit. “By utilizing those unused facilities in Japan, we can stockpile the other countries’ crude oil and in case of crisis... It’s a kind of joint stockpiling system,” he said. Japan has 254 days’ worth of oil reserves, he said, while at the outbreak of the Middle East war in February some ASEAN countries had less than a month’s worth. An ASEAN-backed study for joint stockpiling of oil has also recommended using facilities in Thailand and Indonesia, but Kitamura said a final decision had not been made. “It’s under specific discussion,” Kitamura said. “But as a government in Japan, we are ready to work with ASEAN countries to utilize our own facilities.” Longer term, Tokyo plans to assist ASEAN states to build their own “stockpiling facilities.” “I think this is very important in order to prepare ourselves for future possibilities, crises,” he said. artigo.texto: Spain's government is seeking to tighten restrictions on one of Europe's fastest-growing data center booms, as the country's Socialist prime minister prepares to fight an election. Investors like Amazon, Microsoft and Blackstone-backed QTS are on tenterhooks. The measure, which doesn't need parliamentary approval, could be approved by Pedro Sánchez's cabinet by next week, and is widely expected to pass ahead of the Nov. 29 elections. It could potentially cost one of Europe's fastest-growing tech regions billions of dollars in investment. The government first introduced the decree in August, partly in response to concerns over energy demand and prices. After fierce opposition, it put forward a revised version on Oct. 26, but the proposal still includes strict renewable-energy requirements. "These requirements could pose insurmountable barriers and act as an effective moratorium," S&P said in an October report. The proposed rules would require 80% of electricity used by data centers to come from renewable sources matched hour by hour, with projects potentially losing grid access if they fail to comply. Projects already in development or awaiting grid connections would also be subject to the rules, with a five-year transition period to comply. Data center buildout faces public backlash Data center build-out has quickly become a prominent political issue around the world. In the U.S. midterm elections, CBS exit polls found data centers were a major influence for more than half of voters. In Spain, concerns over the water and energy demands of data centers are increasingly part of the election debate as the country faces mounting pressure to expand its electricity grid to meet the demand. CBRE estimates that while developers have announced 10.5 GW of data center capacity across Spain and Portugal, only about 4.5 GW is currently considered realistically deliverable because of grid, permitting and infrastructure constraints. Alberto Nadal, the opposition center-right Popular Party's deputy secretary for the economy, has said a conservative government would repeal the decree. Recent polling shows the Popular Party leading, with several seat projections putting the PP and far-right Vox together above a parliamentary majority. Aragón at center of debate Aragón, a landlocked region in the country's northeast, governed by the Popular Party, has emerged as one of Europe's fastest-growing digital infrastructure hubs and is at the center of opposition to the draft rules. The region has attracted investors with fast-track permits, abundant renewable energy and land, and international cable connections. Aragón president, Jorge Azcón, wants to turn it into the "Virginia of Europe," referring to the U.S. state with the world's highest density of data center sites. Aragón is set to receive more than 60 billion euros ($66 billion) in data center and digital infrastructure investment over the next decade. But concerns are growing among residents over noise, water use and pressure on the electricity grid. Investment versus resources Pilar Alegría, leader of the Socialist Party in Aragón, told a Nov. 15 rally that the election would be decisive for the region's future and for protecting its natural resources. She highlighted the Ebro River, which runs through Aragón, and raised concerns about the resources used by data centers in a region vulnerable to drought. Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, speaking the same day, sought to reassure investors. "It would be a mistake to squander that advantage through poor planning or regulation that creates uncertainty for investors," Feijóo said. Eva Valle, Aragón's economy minister, has also called for the decree to be scrapped. "It is necessary to halt the approval of this decree, which abounds in harmful conditions placed on the sector," she said at an AWS-organized event on Oct. 27, accusing the government of pursuing "a political agenda." Amazon Web Services and Microsoft have said their investment plans in Aragón remain unchanged, while urging Spain to provide long-term legal certainty and regulatory predictability. Google has already put a multibillion-euro data center project on hold pending greater regulatory certainty, according to a report in Spanish newspaper El Mundo, which cited anonymous sources. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC. SpainDC, which represents the data-center industry in the country, said the decree would give the group's members the most restrictive data center framework in the European Union and could put 80% to 90% of investment at risk. "We are going to use all the institutional, regulatory and legal avenues at our disposal" to challenge the decree, said SpainDC president Emilio Díaz.

artigo.texto: The town doesn’t have a stoplight for traffic — and, as the November 3 election showed, it doesn’t have a red light for data centers either. It was the only place in the country where voters approved one of these facilities, and it wasn’t close: the margin was 3 to 1. The tale is a clue to the future of data centers around the country. Applied Digital, a Dallas-based data center company, wants to build a $3 billion facility in the Harwood area. It would be the largest such facility in the state, covering 1.8 million square feet, the equivalent of 31 football fields. The company had told voters that the alternative was putting the center next door in Fargo, and that convinced Harwoodians that “we might as well get the tax benefits and the tax revenue from it,” as Mayor Blake Hankey put it. He expected the city would get $1.65 million, six times its existing total property tax revenue. And then there were the promised 200 new jobs for the region. Harwood stood in sharp contrast with the rest of the country. Gallup found in March that 71 percent of those surveyed were opposed to data center construction. NBC’s exit polling on November 3 found that data centers were a crucial factor for 69 percent of people voting for Congress. It was little wonder that some of the biggest champions of the centers scurried for cover, including Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro (a Democrat who won big anyway) and Texas Governor Greg Abbott (a Republican who lost by a stunning margin), and who just a year before had proclaimed the state would be the “epicenter of AI development.” Analysts are still sorting out this stunning result, but several things are clear. Local residents didn’t like the idea of big developers draining local water, putting contaminated water back into the ground, gobbling up enormous amounts of electricity, and putting noisy complexes not far from their homes. Frightening warnings that AI is lurking to control us, perhaps somehow building the capacity to kill us all, surely didn’t help. Six in ten Americans are afraid of riding in self-driving cars. It’s broadly ironic that the revolt against technology has happened at precisely the time Americans have become more dependent on the devices in virtually everyone’s pocket. But that’s not all that’s jingling in pockets. A Brookings analyst projected that by 2032, data center and related investment will total $10.3 trillion. That, the Wall Street Journal said, would be “the biggest economic get in US history,” far greater than the Gilded Age railroads or the interstate highway system. Amazon, Microsoft, and Google combined for more than $720 billion in data center investment this year, three times the amount just two years ago. In Texas alone, data center construction accounts for more than one-fourth of the state’s gross domestic product. That sets up a looming dilemma. Harwood voters showed what a green light looks like, but just about everywhere else, voters flashed red. In Texas, Abbott hit a yellow caution light, calling for an audit of planned water and energy usage before giving new centers the green. But Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants red, calling for a complete ban until “laws can be passed by the legislature to protect Texans.” That won’t be easy to do. Democrats won the state house for the first time in 24 years, but Republicans have a comfortable 19-12 margin in the state senate and that’s going to make it hard for the legislature to pass anything restricting data centers. Hinojosa has promised executive action to shut down data center construction, but she can’t do that unilaterally. She’d have to rely instead on three separate regulatory commissions, including the agency regulating the state’s Electric Reliability Council, which is still struggling to right itself after the 2021 weather disaster that almost shut down the state’s whole power grid. The governor gets to make appointments to those commissions, but vacancies occur on a rotating basis and she won’t be able to get controlling appointments for several years. Moreover, appointments to some commissions require senate confirmation, and that’s going to be tough with Republicans holding the upper chamber. And then there’s the tsunami of cash and potential construction jobs building up in every corner of the state. Add the zoning issues lurking in the background. In Texas, for example, cities and towns have zoning power but counties don’t, so if a data center developer plans a project just outside a city limit, there might be nothing to stop it except the property owner’s agreement to sell the property. All these complications make it much harder for the light to stay red for long. One investment bank estimates that perhaps only 2 to 4 percent of planned data centers will ultimately be stopped. With so much money at stake, Harwood’s green light is ultimately the most likely signal to find.

artigo.texto: Data centers: acordo entre Amazon e Blackstone abrange 13 prédios em Indiana e no Mississippi (Adobe Stock/Divulgação) Repórter de Inteligência Artificial e Tecnologia Publicado em 16 de novembro de 2026 às 10h10. Última atualização em 16 de novembro de 2026 às 10h11. A Amazon anunciou em 16 de novembro de 2026 a venda do controle de 13 prédios de data centers nos Estados Unidos, avaliados em US$ 5 bilhões, para a Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC), veículo imobiliário administrado por uma afiliada da Blackstone. A Amazon Web Services (AWS) continuará ocupando todos os imóveis como inquilina, com contratos de prazo médio inicial de 12 anos, que podem chegar a 32 anos com as renovações, e reajuste de 2,75% ao ano. A Amazon receberá dinheiro e ficará com 24,9% das duas sociedades conjuntas que serão donas dos complexos, localizados em Indiana e no Mississippi, que somam 647 megawatts de capacidade. É o primeiro investimento da BXDC desde o IPO, em maio, e a conclusão está prevista para até o fim de 2026. O modelo lembra a sociedade fechada pela Meta com fundos da Blue Owl, em 2025, para o complexo Hyperion, na Louisiana. A Amazon vai passar de proprietária a sócia minoritária e inquilina de 13 prédios de data centers recém-construídos nos Estados Unidos. Em acordo anunciado nesta segunda-feira, 16, um veículo imobiliário administrado por uma afiliada da Blackstone comprará o controle das sociedades que ficarão com os imóveis, avaliados em US$ 5 bilhões. A Amazon Web Services (AWS), braço de computação em nuvem do grupo, vai alugar todos os prédios e continuar usando a infraestrutura. A operação dá à Amazon uma forma de levantar dinheiro com instalações que já construiu e manter a capacidade disponível para seus clientes. Em troca, a companhia assume aluguéis com prazo inicial médio de 12 anos. Se todas as opções de renovação forem exercidas, a média sobe para 32 anos. O reajuste previsto é de 2,75% ao ano, e a própria Amazon garante os pagamentos da subsidiária. Os US$ 5 bilhões correspondem à avaliação bruta dos dois complexos. Na conclusão da operação, a Amazon vai transferir os imóveis para duas sociedades conjuntas, uma para cada complexo, e receber dinheiro e uma fatia de 24,9% em cada uma. A Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, negociada na Bolsa de Nova York sob o código BXDC, ficará com os outros 75,1%. O pagamento em dinheiro será financiado por duas fontes. A BXDC espera aportar US$ 1,9 bilhão em recursos levantados no IPO. Subsidiárias das sociedades conjuntas devem contratar cerca de US$ 2,5 bilhões em empréstimos hipotecários, garantidos pelos próprios imóveis. Como parte do financiamento também cobrirá custos da transação, a soma dessas duas fontes indica o volume de recursos mobilizados, e o valor líquido a ser recebido pela Amazon ainda depende dos termos do fechamento. É o primeiro investimento da BXDC desde a abertura de capital, em maio. A oferta inicial foi de US$ 1,75 bilhão e, depois que os bancos exerceram integralmente a opção de vender ações adicionais, a captação líquida chegou a cerca de US$ 1,9 bilhão. A conclusão da compra está prevista para até o fim de 2026, sujeita às condições do acordo. O acordo reúne nove prédios no norte de Indiana, no mercado de data centers da região de Chicago, e quatro no Mississippi. Juntos, eles somam 647 megawatts de capacidade elétrica para equipamentos de TI. O número indica a potência que a infraestrutura pode disponibilizar a equipamentos como servidores e sistemas de rede. Para a BXDC, a compra dá acesso a prédios novos com um contrato para ocupar 100% do portfólio. Para a AWS, a locação mantém disponíveis os imóveis de que a operação depende. O contrato segue o modelo conhecido como triple net, em que o inquilino arca, além do aluguel, com despesas como impostos imobiliários, seguro e manutenção. A aquisição foi precificada a uma taxa inicial de capitalização de 7%. O indicador relaciona a renda operacional anual dos imóveis ao valor atribuído a eles. Ele serve para avaliar o preço pago pelo portfólio. O retorno para o acionista da BXDC também depende do custo da dívida e das demais despesas da operação. A parceria permite à Amazon recuperar parte do capital investido nas instalações e continuar usando os prédios. O dinheiro entra no fechamento. Os aluguéis serão pagos ao longo dos anos, com reajuste anual. Para o investidor imobiliário, o atrativo é justamente o fluxo de pagamentos de uma única locatária, respaldado pela garantia da Amazon. Prasad Kalyanaraman, vice-presidente de infraestrutura da AWS, afirmou no comunicado que a parceria permite à empresa continuar ampliando sua operação à medida que cresce a demanda dos clientes. No terceiro trimestre, a receita da AWS cresceu 39%, para US$ 46 bilhões. A expansão exige investimentos em terrenos, energia e prédios, além dos chips e servidores instalados neles. O acordo com a Blackstone traz um investidor para a parte imobiliária dessa conta. A Meta recorreu a uma sociedade com fundos da Blue Owl em outubro de 2025 para desenvolver o complexo Hyperion, na Louisiana. Os fundos ficaram com 80%, e a Meta, com 20%. Os US$ 27 bilhões divulgados naquele acordo correspondem ao custo estimado de desenvolvimento, incluindo construção e infraestrutura de energia, refrigeração e conectividade. No caso da Amazon, os US$ 5 bilhões são a avaliação de imóveis já construídos, que a AWS continuará usando como inquilina. A AWS vai alugar todos os 13 prédios. A Amazon também manterá 24,9% das sociedades que serão donas dos imóveis. Os US$ 5 bilhões são o valor bruto atribuído aos dois complexos. Na conclusão do negócio, a Amazon receberá uma parcela em dinheiro e manterá uma participação minoritária nas sociedades. A BXDC espera concluir a transação até o fim de 2026. O fechamento depende das condições do acordo e do financiamento previsto. artigo.texto: Data center moratorium extension recommended for Bloomington BLOOMINGTON (25News Now) -Bloomington’s planning commission recommends pushing the data center moratorium out for another 12 months. Since the first public event, staff made several changes to their proposed rules, based on public feedback. The commission voted to recommend extending the current moratorium for a year, instead of another six months, to come up with data center regulations. Some of the proposed changes include banning non-disclosure agreements about data centers, no matter what size the center would be, and higher fines for developers who violate city regulations. Some stakeholders, like the Citizens’ Utility Board, sent a representative who said he was pleased with proposed regulations on energy. “Relating to the energy use provisions of the ordinance, I’ve read through the draft, and I find them to be more than reasonable, really, they look a lot better than other ordinances I’ve seen around the state,” said Scott Allen of CUB. The planning commission recommended the moratorium that expires on Nov. 27 should be extended for a year, but the city council will take final action on that. artigo.texto: Data center moratorium passes in Michigan City MICHIGAN CITY, Ind (WSBT) — Michigan City pressing pause on new data center development. The Common Council approved a temporary moratorium Tuesday night. But, Google's project already under construction is exempt, raising questions from residents. Protesters gathered outside City Hall before the vote calling for stronger environmental protections. While the council approved the moratorium, protestors are more worried about the google development already underway. The newly approved ordinance temporarily blocks permits and other city approvals for future data center projects. Council members also discussed the need for equipment and safeguards to address noise and air pollution. With equipment, applied for a fine exhaust, for noise, so that the exhaust isn’t going to be polluting the air around the development, into the neighborhood, into the schools that are around there and just making the whole quality of life issue better for everybody. Donald Pryzbylinski, Michigan City Common Council The ordinance requires two public workshops within 90 days, giving residents a chance to weigh in on future zoning and environmental regulations.

artigo.texto: German energy giant RWE has just broken ground on a colossal 262.5-megawatt-hour (MWh) battery that is capable of supplying roughly 21,000 households with electricity during peak evening hours. The 62.5-megawatt (MW) battery is reportedly RWE’s first battery energy storage system (BESS) in Italy. Located in the city of Ragusa in Sicily, it will be fitted with 42 containers housing lithium-ion batteries. RWE representatives revealed that the system will have a total storage capacity of 262.5 megawatt-hours (MWh). It will be capable of delivering its maximum output for four hours. This will be enough to cover the evening peak electricity demand of around 21,000 Italian households. The company expects to commission the project by the end of 2027. “The start of construction of our Ragusa battery storage marks an important milestone,” Sopna Sury, CEO of RWE Renewables Europe & Australia, said. “We have been operating in Italy for many years, using the energy from the wind and the sun.” Power for peak demand Sury explained that the battery will support the balance between electricity supply and demand. “In a world of growing renewable energy, battery storage systems are crucial for stabilizing the grid and ensuring that electricity is used when it is needed most,” Sury continued. More from Energy See All Unlike conventional power plants, renewable energy sources depend on weather conditions. Battery storage systems can store excess electricity when production is high and release it when the demand increases. RWE said its new battery will provide balancing energy to stabilize the electricity grid. It will also feature technology capable of delivering grid-forming services such as instantaneous reserve, also known as inertia. Apart from installing the batteries, RWE will build the necessary grid infrastructure, including a high-voltage transformer that will link the system to the 150-kilovolt (kV) electricity grid. “[The] Ragusa battery will be capable of covering the evening peak demand of around 21.000 households for four hours,” Sury added. More battery capacity With the project, RWE aims to expand its battery storage business across Europe and other parts of the world. The company currently operates approximately 1.7 gigawatts (GW) of battery storage capacity worldwide. At the same time, another three GW are under construction. Additionally, RWE has established a strong presence in Italy’s renewable energy market. It currently operates 18 onshore wind farms, one solar power plant, and three agrivoltaic facilities. Together, these projects have an installed capacity of approximately 670 MW. This is enough to supply renewable electricity to more than 550,000 Italian households. The company is also constructing 200 MW of additional wind and solar capacity across the country. The Ragusa project will complement these renewable energy operations. Meanwhile, RWE plans to develop further battery storage capacity in Italy alongside its existing wind and solar projects. “We look forward to establishing further battery storage capacity in Italy soon – in addition to wind and solar power – in order to support Italy in building a resilient energy system,” Sury said in a press release. He explained that the expansion will make Italy’s electricity grid more reliable.

artigo.texto: Korea has joined the Carbon Market Club of Clubs (OCCCM), an international coalition on carbon markets that includes the European Union (EU) and China. With this, Korea will take part in talks that set rules for the international carbon market, including internationally transferred mitigation outcomes and offset credits. Kim Sunghwan, Minister of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, announced Korea's entry at a high-level meeting of the Carbon Market Club of Clubs held on the sidelines of the 31st U.N. Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, on the 16th local time. The Carbon Market Club of Clubs is an international cooperation body that shares experience operating compliance carbon markets such as emissions trading systems and carbon taxes, and discusses measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), carbon accounting, and high-quality offset systems. Brazil proposed creating the group at COP30 last year, and it launched in May this year with the EU, China, and other major operators of carbon markets at its core. Korea joined after receiving an invitation from the EU as a follow-up to Korea-EU summit diplomacy in June. Membership is open to countries or regional economic integration organizations that operate or are developing a domestic compliance carbon market or carbon pricing system. Members have voting rights at high-level meetings. Announcing the accession, Minister Kim said, "Korea was the first in East Asia to introduce and operate a nationwide emissions trading system in 2015," adding, "We now manage more than 70% of the country's greenhouse gas emissions." He added, "We will share with member states our MRV system built for a manufacturing-centered industrial structure, our market design and operation, and our experience running an offset program within the ETS." Kim also said Korea is working to shift from a fossil fuel–based economy to an 'electric nation' centered on zero-carbon power, and introduced the government's Korea Green Transformation (K-GX) strategy released last month. By joining, Korea can now take part in setting international carbon market rules, including creating internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and establishing common principles for high-integrity offset credits. Meanwhile, the high-level meeting adopted the 'COP31 Carbon Market Club of Clubs Declaration,' which welcomes new members and commits to developing the coalition into a core consultative body for international cooperation on compliance carbon markets.
